as_told.title: Gnostic reading that Jesus survived the crucifixion

plain: Some say Jesus did not die on the cross in Jerusalem, and that the Last Supper and the crucifixion were a planned and staged ritual in which he was drugged and later brought back round. Jesse Michels describes it as a Gnostic reading of the New Testament, Gnostic meaning early Christian groups whose writings were left out of the Bible. He cites the Gospel of Thomas, one of those writings, along with the religion scholar Elaine Pagels and the writer Brian Muraresku, author of The Immortality Key. In a separate conversation the researcher Randall Carlson tells Michels, without naming a single source, that Jesus did not die on the cross and that "there was a lot more to the story going on behind the scenes," and he mentions Muraresku and the Gospel figure Joseph of Arimathea. If true, the central event of Christianity would have been a carefully staged rite.
